# #748 — 62 catch sites swallow errors without logging or re-raising (STANDARDS-observability violation)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-25T12:06:49Z
Updated: 2026-08-25T12:06:49Z

---

## What

An audit during #747 found catch sites in `src/` and `server/` that neither log
nor re-raise, which `_DOCS/STANDARDS-observability.md` (`### Never swallow an
error`) forbids:

> Every caught exception is logged at an appropriate level, then either
> re-raised or handled. **Catch blocks that return a fallback value must log
> before returning.** Never `catch { return null }` silently. A bound-but-
> unlogged catch (`catch (e) {}` with no logging) is the same violation as an
> empty one; linting for empty blocks alone is insufficient.

## Measurement

Brace-matched scan of all 246 non-test TypeScript files in `src/` and
`server/`, counting catch bodies containing no `logger.`/`log.` call, no
`throw`, and no `reject`:

```
total catch sites scanned in 246 files
swallowing (no log, no throw): 62
```

**62 is the audit ceiling, not the violation count.** A meaningful number
report through a helper the scan cannot see -- `reportSinkFailure`
(`src/rotating-file.ts`), `noteSkip` (`src/drop-folder-collector.ts`),
`logDurableLaneFailure`, `logRecallFailure` -- and those are compliant. The
list needs triage per site, not a bulk edit.

Sites with no visible reporting path, as candidates for that triage:

```
server/config/nats.ts:91                  return "url_unparseable";
server/main.ts:395                        <EMPTY>
server/observability/langfuse-tracing.ts:228   return undefined;
server/observability/langfuse-tracing.ts:1462  return;
server/realtime/recovery-wal.ts:737       return null;
server/tools/entry-text.ts:23             return [];
server/transport/server-identity.ts:132   return [];
server/transport/server-identity.ts:227   return undefined;
src/embedding-canonical.ts:61             return [];
src/embedding-canonical.ts:87             return true;
src/logger.ts:120                         return "unknown";
src/logger.ts:265                         return {};
src/logger.ts:501                         <EMPTY>
src/logger.ts:577                         <EMPTY>
src/nats-bridge.ts:474                    return [];
src/realtime/recovery-wal.ts:681          return null;
src/tools/repo-facts.ts:78                return false;
```

Some of these are almost certainly correct as-is -- `src/logger.ts` cannot log
its own failure without recursing, which is exactly the kind of case the
standard means by "documented decision in the code". The work is deciding
per site and writing the decision down, not silencing the scan.

## Why it matters here specifically

#747 is a four-defect chain in which every layer returned cleanly while doing
nothing, and the pipeline starved for 27 days with no error anywhere. One of
the 62 was introduced during that fix: the backlog probe caught and set `null`
with no log, which would have recreated the silent-fallback defect *inside the
detector built to catch it*. Fixed in `a61b99d`.

That is the cost of the pattern in this codebase, measured rather than
asserted.

## Scope

- Triage each site: real violation, or fail-open that needs its documented
  decision written in the code.
- Fix the real ones by logging before the fallback return.
- Add the enforcement the standard calls for: "every catch/except body
  contains a log call or a re-raise -- a custom rule; stock no-empty-block
  checks miss the bound-but-unlogged case." Without the lint rule this
  regresses.

## Not in scope

Behaviour changes. A swallowed error becomes a logged one; whether the
fallback itself is right is a separate question per site.

## Receipts

Scan reproducible from the repo root; #747 carries the full context and the
one fix already applied.
